 Net interest margin was pressured by a $2.1 million interest income reversal, which reduced the reported NIM from a normalized 3.60% to 3.49%. 
 Management maintains an asset-sensitive posture, indicating that any future Federal Reserve rate hikes would likely provide a further benefit to the net interest margin. 
 Deposit growth of 1.2% was achieved through disciplined pricing, though management acknowledged this discipline likely constrained overall growth in a highly competitive market. 
 The bank is facing unconventional competition from Treasuries, as customers leverage the tax-exempt status of Treasury yields to achieve higher effective returns than traditional bank products. 
 Loan balances saw a slight decrease due to a large credit being moved to for-sale status and unexpected payoffs, despite a solid underlying pipeline. 
 Nonaccrual loan levels remain 'stubborn' due to court-related delays in bankruptcy proceedings, pushing several expected resolutions into late 2027. 
 Operational efficiency remains a priority, with management successfully controlling overhead and reducing professional service fees despite inflationary pressures. 
 Outlook and Strategic Initiatives 
 Management anticipates a solid rebound in loan growth for the fourth quarter of 2026, supported by a robust pipeline of delayed projects. 
 The competitive deposit environment is expected to persist well into 2027, driven by both non-bank institutions and the attractive yields of government securities. 
 Expense guidance for the fourth quarter is projected between $23 million and $24 million, reflecting normalized legal and incentive compensation costs. 
 The bank expects a strong 2027 economic environment and a relatively stable interest rate market to support long-term performance. 
 Strategic focus remains on the gradual improvement of non-interest income and the resolution of the remaining $177.6 million in classified loans. 
 Risk Factors and Structural Adjustments 
 A $2.1 million recovery of interest income reversal acted as a one-time headwind to third-quarter earnings and margin metrics. 
 Classified loans totaled $177.6 million at quarter-end, including $11.5 million in Other Real Estate Owned (OREO). 
 Legal and bankruptcy court proceedings are the primary bottleneck for credit resolution, with some timelines extending nearly a year beyond original expectations. 
 Management noted a migration slowdown in credit quality, with only $20 million in new credits classified as substandard while remaining on accrual status.

 Deposit beta and pricing discipline in a rising rate environment

 Management expects deposit beta to be significantly slower on the way up, noting they decreased total deposit costs by 3 basis points this quarter despite market pressure. 
 The bank is prioritizing cost control over aggressive growth, even if it results in more modest deposit inflows. 
 Timeline and strategy for resolving nonperforming assets (NPAs) 
 Resolution of large loans is currently subject to bankruptcy court decisions; if court-approved sales continue to stall, the bank intends to foreclose and dispose of the properties independently. 
 Management expressed confidence in full recovery for several credits due to favorable loan-to-value ratios on the underlying collateral. 
 Drivers of loan growth volatility and pipeline health 
 The third-quarter slowdown was attributed to a combination of unexpected payoffs and customers being more conscientious about project viability at higher interest rates. 
 The fourth-quarter pipeline is described as stronger due to the carryover of delayed fundings from the previous period. 
 Impact of Treasury yields on core deposit retention 
 Management highlighted that a 5% Treasury yield effectively equals 5.65% for California residents due to state tax exemptions, creating a significant hurdle for bank CD retention. 
 The bank is seeing a trend of customers moving funds into Treasuries immediately following the maturity of their certificates of deposit.
